Dressmaker Patch Notes and Update History

Last updated September 21, 2026. Dressmaker is a fan-made guide and is not affiliated with the developers.

Dressmaker has a longer public paper trail than most cozy games its size. Its first patch note appeared on August 4, 2025, five numbered prototype patches followed within two months, the builds then went quiet for half a year, and the full game reached Steam on September 21, 2026. This page records all of it for the dressmaker game, newest first.

Two caveats. This log is kept by hand by a fan site, not by the developers, and the official Steam news hub is authoritative — where the two disagree, Steam is right. And as of September 21, 2026 there is no post-launch patch: the only thing Steam carries from launch day is the launch announcement.

Steam release era (April to September 2026)

Everything in this section was announced on the Steam news hub. From April 2026 the same posts were mirrored to the itch.io devlog, often days later; the Steam date is used here.

September 21, 2026 — Launch day, and no patch yet

Dressmaker is out on Steam for Windows and macOS at $14.99, with a 10% launch discount to $13.49. The only post published that day was the launch announcement itself, so there is no patch to report here. It promises small fixes "in the immediate weeks" with "a sprinkling of new fabrics and accessories", and names what is further off: a challenge mode where players vote on each other's dresses, transparent fabrics, proper controller support, and mobile and Switch ports. Source: the Steam news hub.

September 7, 2026 — Scalding September Tea: the price, and what is not in the box

Two weeks before launch the developers said the number out loud: $14.99, with regional pricing and a -10% launch discount. The post also ruled out microtransactions, ads, data harvesting and generative AI, and put figures on the build — roughly 35 hours of story commissions, 150 dress pieces, 450 fabrics and 350 accessories. Source: the price announcement on itch.io.

August 31, 2026 — August Tea: content complete, three weeks out

With three weeks to go the team confirmed the date would be met and the game was already content complete: credits compiled, ending finished, achievement icons painted. It is also where the team is named, three full-time developers with almost 40 years of combined experience, plus collaborators on sound, art, testing and music. Source: the Steam news hub.

July 28, 2026 — July Tea: the launch date arrives

The wishlist count passed 200,000 and the release date was pinned down: September 21, 2026. The post opened early-build sign-ups for creators under embargo and showed a brighter, more open front desk. Source: the July Tea on itch.io.

June 9, 2026 — Dressmaker passes 100,000 wishlists

A milestone post and nothing else. The developers credited prototype players who left detailed comments and screenshots, saying that enthusiasm convinced the people holding the purse strings to greenlight the full game. Source: the Steam news hub.

June 6, 2026 — Wholesome Direct trailer and a September window

A new trailer dropped during Wholesome Direct, announcing a September 2026 launch window rather than a date. That trailer is the one the Steam store page now lists as the release trailer. Source: the Steam news hub.

May 27, 2026 — May Tea: a new fabric inventory and off-rack dresses

A fabric inventory rework that shows silk and velvet highlights more accurately, and hides the full fabric name until you hover. The team also described making your own dresses to sell off the rack, and said nine of ten planned characters were illustrated. The itch.io version arrived late, as "Belated May Tea" on June 3, 2026. Source: the Steam news hub.

April 15, 2026 — April Tea: the full game stops looking like the prototype

The first substantial look at the built-from-scratch version. Characters are measured and the mannequin adjusted to fit, with pattern pieces drafted to match. New shaders give silk and velvet different kinds of shine, and the fabric shop was rebuilt to feel like a haberdashery rather than a grid of buttons. The itch.io edition landed on April 17, 2026. Source: the Steam news hub.

Prototype era: the 2025 patch run

Everything below is a build update for the free prototype, numbered with its own scheme. The newest files on the itch.io page are still labelled 0.5.5, so nothing here has been replaced by a later prototype build.

November 11, 2025 — "We've gone quiet!"

The last post of the prototype era, and there is no patch in it. sarandipityx explained that updates had stopped while the team worked on the full game, and asked readers to wishlist the Steam page. The silence lasted until April 2026. Source: itch.io devlog.

October 3, 2025 — Hotfix 0.5.5

Two fixes: flounce sleeves were showing the three-quarter sleeve sprite in the sketchbook, and the ruffle skirt had the wrong grainline and name. That repair broke panel ordering on skirts players had already made. The team admitted they had been "a bit messy" about preserving prototype saves. Source: itch.io devlog.

September 29, 2025 — Hotfix 0.5.3

The busiest patch of the run. Trim placement became less finicky, the mannequin scene gained middle-click zoom, and the ruffle skirt — nicknamed "the megaskirt" — was rebuilt with equal side panels, which did break dresses already made with it. It also added needle and pin models, Argyle wool, a new red silk and a Gothic Collar pattern, before a follow-up fixed a save-corruption bug. Source: itch.io devlog.

September 23, 2025 — Update 0.5.1: new content and a long fix list

A new bodice and skirt arrived, with the warning that the skirt "may genuinely require in the region of about 40m of fabric to cut". Pattern panels started showing seam allowances, an inventory menu replaced cycling through fabrics, and new trims were added. Fixes covered trim usability, false sewing direction detection, upside-down patterns and a colour picker glitch. Source: itch.io devlog.

September 18, 2025 — The Steam page goes live

The Dressmaker Steam page appeared with wishlisting open, alongside a substantial prototype update. The highlights were, in the developers' words, too many to list: easier sewing, more accessories, more fabrics, one new skirt, and lace trim you could finally add to a finished dress. Source: itch.io devlog.

September 9, 2025 — Hotfix: keyboard controls for sewing

Keyboard controls arrived for sewing, bound to SPACE and the arrow keys, with more consistent mouse sensitivity and a more forgiving sewing line. The patch fixed the newspaper reappearing, pattern panels showing up when switching fabrics, and odd behaviour when interacting with a panel mid-animation. Source: itch.io devlog.

September 5, 2025 — Greenlit, and a sketchbook preview

A small update carrying the year's biggest news. A sketchbook preview now sits beside the cutting room table, and the shop gained new buttons. The developers confirmed Free Lives had greenlit the full game — the numbers were decent, but the passionate comments decided it. Source: itch.io devlog.

September 2 and 3, 2025 — Patches 0.4.1 and 0.4.2

Two patches in two days. The first fixed incorrect scoring, stopped the shop breaking at the end of the prototype, and repaired the butterfly and Juliette sleeves. The second was an emergency fix for a bug that made the fourth dress — the one that needs bows — almost impossible to finish. Source: itch.io devlog.

September 1, 2025 — Big update, and some mixed news

The update that made the prototype worth getting attached to: buttons and bows after sewing, a pageable history of your previous dresses, and panel-by-panel colouring. Sewing was reworked with a speed control, and a new character arrived with two quests. The post also admitted downloads were not yet high enough to make funding an easy yes. Source: itch.io devlog.

August 4, 2025 — The first patch

The oldest post on the devlog, and the first clean-up pass on a prototype built, in the developers' words, in "a very quick, dirty manner". Reset Save now actually reset your save, sewing became a little more forgiving, and the confetti audio was made much less jarring. Source: itch.io devlog.

Where the next Dressmaker patch will show up

Patches for the released game appear on the Steam news hub first, and that is the page to follow. The itch.io devlog records the prototype only, and its newest build is still 0.5.5; the developers have not said whether the free prototype will get further updates.

The launch post promises small fixes plus extra fabrics and accessories soon, so this page will be updated as those land. If something breaks in the meantime, the Dressmaker troubleshooting page covers the common ones. For the launch itself, see Dressmaker release date; for the free prototype, see the Dressmaker demo page.
